classification.difficultyReason: Link the tangent–radius right angle to equal base angles and a triangle sum, and separately use the alternate segment theorem for the circumference angle.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Inscribed triangle with top, right and lower-left vertices; tangent PQ at the right vertex; centre O and dashed radii to the top and right vertices. Ordinary source hues are replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: The upward tangent and top-right chord form 38 degrees. x lies between that chord and the radius at the right vertex; y is the corresponding base angle at the top; z is the central angle between the dashed radii; w is the inscribed angle at the lower-left vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 38-degree angle is visible; x, y, z and w remain unknown.

answer.worked:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
$$\begin{align*}x+38^\circ&=90^\circ\\x&=52^\circ\end{align*}$$
The dashed radii are equal, so the base angles of the isosceles triangle are equal.
$$y=52^\circ$$
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}z+52^\circ+52^\circ&=180^\circ\\z&=76^\circ\end{align*}$$
By the alternate segment theorem,
$$w=38^\circ.$$
